title: Configuration
body: `docc.json` is optional and every field has a default. The nearest `docc.json` is used: it is looked up in the current folder, then in the parent folders, and its folder becomes the project root, so docc can run from a subfolder. If there is none, the current folder is the root and the defaults apply; `docc init` does not look upward. Unknown keys are errors, reported as docc.json:line:column: config error: message with exit code 2. `docc schema config` prints the full schema. ^CON-1

Paths: `src`, `out`, `schemas` and `outFull`. The folder `out` is owned by docc: the build deletes every file in it that no source produced. Folders that overlap the sources, the schemas or the project root are refused. ^CON-2

`roots` lists the ids from which reachability is counted, default `index`. `tree` says what the document tree is: `parents` (the default) nests the documents by their parent below the roots; `folders` makes it the folders of the source folder. In folder mode `roots`, DOC203 and DOC205 do not apply, since every document is in the tree, and `parent` still gives the breadcrumbs. A folder's own page is the document named like the folder inside it (`decisions/decisions.json`): its title and order are the folder's; without one the folder shows its name. An own page without text (no body or an empty one, and no free field, only service fields such as title, kind, order and tags) is a title-only folder page: it only names and orders its folder and gets no page in the output, neither a file in the output folder nor a page in the one-file builds. The folder then shows that title without a link, a link `[[id]]` to it reads as the title without a link, and a parent pointing at it gives no breadcrumbs; `docc compile` keeps it among its pages and as the id of the folder. Not `index.json`: ids are unique in the whole project, and every folder would hold one. Folders and documents of one folder sort together by `order`, then by title, then by name, and numbering follows the folders. `tags` is an optional registry of allowed tags, checked by DOC107. Kinds have no registry: a kind exists when its schema file exists in the schemas folder. ^CON-3

`rules` maps a rule name (such as style/hedging), a group name or a code (DOC352, which gives DOC902) to a level or to an object with a level and the parameters `words` and `allow` of the word rules. A rule is more specific than its group, and a group is more specific than the preset. `recommended` set to `false` turns the preset off; core rules stay on. `maxWarnings` sets the warning limit of every command. `commitOut` (default `true`) says whether `docs/out` is committed: with `false` it is built for reading but kept out of git, DOC501 does not apply, and `docc init` writes it so and adds the folder to `.gitignore`. The key `changesSince` is gone: an old `docc.json` with it gets an error naming `docc build --html --since <revision>`, which sets the version the HTML file shows the edits from. ^CON-4
`customRules` define rules as a regular expression over a JSON pointer: forbid a match or require one. ^CON-5

`numbering` set to `true` makes docc number the pages and their sections, as described in [[rendering@67mw]]. `lang` is `en` (the default) or `ru` and sets the language of the fixed labels of the pages. ^CON-6

`branding` (name, url, logo, accent, accentLight, header) dresses the single HTML file for a company, as described in [[rendering@67mw]]; `name` is required, the logo is a file inside the project and must exist. ^CON-7

`trace.scan` lists masks of code files, from the project root, that are searched for `docc:` tags; without it DOC401 to DOC404 do not run. Masks reach into git submodules: the files of a submodule are listed by its own git, with its own ignores, and a Git hook's environment (GIT_DIR and the like) does not change which repository is read. A mask that matches nothing is no error. ^CON-8
